===============================================================================
RESIDENTIAL DWELLING INSURANCE
GENERAL POLICY CONDITIONS - PROPERTY DAMAGE COVER
===============================================================================

These conditions apply together with the General Contract Provisions and with
the Schedule, both of which form part of this contract. Sums insured, limits,
deductibles, periods and percentages shown in square brackets are those stated
in the Schedule.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 1 - PURPOSE AND KEY CONCEPTS
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

1.1 What this insurance does

Combined residential buildings insurance protects the policyholder against the
financial consequences of physical damage to their building. The perils that can
be insured are the ones bundled together in these conditions - fire, escape of
water, storm and hail, and further natural hazards among them. Which of the
insurable perils are actually covered is agreed between insurer and policyholder
and recorded in the schedule.

Where insured property is destroyed or damaged, the insurer indemnifies the cost
of putting it back in the same kind and quality. The technical plant that serves
the building, and the electrical installation belonging to it, share in that
cover. A range of consequential expenses triggered by a loss event - the removal
of what the event destroyed, and the measures taken immediately to limit the
damage, among them - is also carried.

1.2 How the wording is to be read

Personal designations are to be understood as gender-neutral throughout; no
parallel male and female forms are used.

1.3 Explanation of recurring terms (not legally binding)

Policyholder - the insurer's contracting party and the purchaser of the cover.

Insured event - the event for which the insurer pays.

Affected part - a room, a surface, a building component, an installation or an
item in which physical damage caused by the insured event has been established by
the loss investigation. The affected parts, taken together, delimit what the
insurer indemnifies.

Repair cost - outlay that serves to put an affected part back into the condition
it was in immediately before the insured event, or to put a destroyed
installation back into service. Outlay that serves another purpose -
preservation, upkeep, protection against future influences, or the running of a
contractor's business - is not a repair cost, whatever heading it is invoiced
under.

Plant of the building - the installations that are permanently connected to the
building, serve its supply, its heating, its ventilation, its water or its power,
and remain in place once the work is finished. Heat generators, heat pumps,
storage vessels, exhaust and flue routes, permanently installed circulating and
lifting pumps, control equipment and the electrical installation are plant of the
building. Plant of the building is insured property; it is replaced, not hired.

Working equipment - the devices, appliances, machines, pumps and comparable items
that a contractor brings to the insured site in order to carry out an operation,
and that are taken away again once the operation is finished. Working equipment
does not become part of the building and is not insured property, whether it is
described as hired, deployed, supplied or procured.

Measure - an operation billed by reference to what is achieved, rather than by
reference to the items used to achieve it. The removal of standing water is an
example.

Combined position - a single line of an invoice that covers more than one
operation, more than one installation or more than one part of the insured
property, and that does not state separately what falls to each.

Exclusion - a peril, a type of damage, an item of property or a type of outlay
for which no cover exists.

Duties - the things the policyholder must do or refrain from doing before, during
and after an insured event.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 2 - INSURED PERILS
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

2.1 The perils that can be covered

The insurer indemnifies insured property that is destroyed or damaged by, or lost
as a consequence of, the following events:

  (a) FIRE GROUP - fire; lightning strike; overvoltage caused by lightning;
      explosion; deflagration; implosion; impact or crash of an aircraft, its
      parts or its cargo; impact of a vehicle; scorching; smoke and soot.

  (b) ESCAPE OF WATER.

  (c) NATURAL HAZARDS, in two tiers:
        (c1) storm and hail;
        (c2) the further natural hazards - flood, backing-up of water,
             earthquake, ground subsidence, landslip, snow load, avalanche and
             volcanic eruption.

2.2 How the groups combine

Each of the three groups (a), (b) and (c1) can be taken separately. The further
natural hazards under (c2) can only be taken in combination with one or more of
the perils in (a), (b) or (c1); they are not available on a standalone basis.

2.4 Escape of water defined

2.4.1 The three headings
The escape of water peril covers three things: escape of water damage; fracture
damage to pipework inside buildings; and fracture damage to pipework outside
buildings.

2.4.2 Escape of water damage
Escaping water means water that has emerged contrary to its intended purpose
from:
  (a) pipes of the water supply, whether supply or drainage lines, or hoses
      connected to them;
  (b) other installations connected to those pipes or hoses, or the
      water-carrying parts of such installations;
  (c) heating or air-conditioning systems;
  (d) water-based extinguishing or sprinkler systems;
  (e) water beds or aquaria.

Operating fluids from heating or air-conditioning systems, and steam, also count
as escaping water. Fluids intended for the generation of energy do not.

2.4.3 Fracture damage to pipework inside buildings
Covered inside buildings: frost-related and other fracture damage to the pipes of
the water and gas supply, of heating and air-conditioning systems, of
water-based extinguishing or sprinkler systems and of rainwater drainage,
together with the fittings, valves, vessels and connection elements belonging to
them.

2.4.5 Plant and the electrical installation
Damage to the plant of the building within the meaning of 1.3 is covered where
that damage was caused by the insured event. This extends to the whole of an
installation where its parts form one functional unit and the unit cannot be
brought back into service by replacing a single part.

The same applies to the electrical installation of the building - circuits,
cabling, distribution boards, terminals, protective and switching devices -
insofar as it was exposed to the escaping water, and to the labour of
establishing which of its parts were affected.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 3 - EXCLUSIONS
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

3.1 General exclusions

3.1.1 War
Damage caused by war, warlike events, civil war, revolution, rebellion or
insurrection is not covered. This applies irrespective of any contributing
causes.

3.1.2 Civil commotion
Damage caused by internal civil unrest is not covered. This applies irrespective
of any contributing causes.

3.1.3 Nuclear energy
Damage caused by nuclear energy, nuclear radiation or radioactive substances is
not covered. This applies irrespective of any contributing causes.

3.3 Exclusions within the escape of water peril

Damage caused by the following is not covered, irrespective of any contributing
causes except where such causes are named below:
  (a) splash water or cleaning water;
  (b) dry rot and house-rot fungi of every kind;
  (c) groundwater, standing or flowing surface water, flood, precipitation, or a
      backing-up of water brought about by any of these causes;
  (d) earthquake, snow load, avalanche, volcanic eruption;
  (e) ground subsidence or landslip - unless escaping water within the meaning of
      2.4.2 caused the subsidence or the landslip;
  (f) the perils of the fire group;
  (g) storm, hail.

Damage to buildings or parts of buildings that are not ready for occupation is
not covered.

3.5 Work beyond the affected parts, and outlay that is not a repair cost

Work carried out beyond those parts of the insured property that were themselves
affected by the insured event is not covered. Outlay that does not constitute a
repair cost is not indemnified. The delimitation in each case is governed by
7.1.5 to 7.1.10.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 4 - INSURED PROPERTY, INSURED LOCATION, DEDUCTIBLES
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

4.1 What is insured

Insured property comprises:
  (a) the buildings identified in the schedule;
  (b) their building components;
  (c) their building accessories;
  (d) terraces on the insured site that directly adjoin the building;
  (e) further site installations.

4.2 The categories defined

4.2.1 Building and dwelling
Buildings are structures connected to the ground. They must be capable of
affording protection against external influences and, for the purposes of these
conditions, must be intended for predominantly residential use.

4.2.2 Building components
Building components are items incorporated into a building that have lost their
independence through their firm connection with it. The plant of the building
within the meaning of 1.3 counts as a building component, together with the
pipework, cabling, connection and discharge elements by which it is joined to the
building, and the housings, mountings and bases on which it stands.

4.2.3 Building accessories
Building accessories are movable items located inside the building or attached to
its exterior that serve the upkeep of the insured building or its predominant
intended purpose.

4.3 Property not insured

Not insured:
  (a) photovoltaic installations and their components;
  (b) all items subsequently incorporated into the building by a tenant or by a
      condominium owner where that person both procured or took the items over at
      their own expense and bears the risk for them;
  (c) electronically stored data and programs;
  (d) working equipment within the meaning of 1.3, irrespective of who brings it
      to the insured site, of how it is charged, and of whether it is hired or
      purchased for the occasion. Its treatment is governed by 5.2.2 and
      7.1.8(b).

4.5 The insured location

The insured location is the insured site: the land parcel on which the insured
building stands, together with the building and its ancillary and technical
rooms.

4.7 Deductibles

A deductible is the share of the indemnity, or the amount, that the policyholder
bears itself per insured event. The deductible stated in the schedule is deducted
once from the indemnity for the insured event, irrespective of how many trades,
invoices or heads of claim are involved.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 5 - INSURED COSTS, LOSS OF RENT AND RENTAL VALUE
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

5.1 Which costs are covered

The insurer reimburses the following costs where they were necessary as a
consequence of an insured event and were actually incurred:
  (a) debris removal, dismantling and disposal costs;
  (b) costs of emergency and loss-mitigation measures;
  (c) costs of moving and protecting property;
  (d) costs of lost water, gas and heating oil, and of electricity lost from
      storage installations;
  (e) hotel costs;
  (f) costs of returning early from a holiday.

Reimbursement of each of these heads is limited to the amount agreed for it.

5.2 The cost heads defined

5.2.1 Debris removal, dismantling and disposal
Costs incurred in clearing away and demolishing insured property. This includes
the expense of removing the remains of that property, transporting them to the
nearest disposal site, depositing them and destroying them.

Plant and installations that the insured event has rendered unusable fall under
this head, together with the work of disconnecting and taking them out. It is
immaterial whether the material to be removed arose from the damage itself or
from the repair work carried out because of it.

5.2.2 Emergency and loss-mitigation measures
Costs of the measures reasonably taken to stop the ingress or spread of water, to
remove standing water from rooms, voids and shafts, and to prevent further
damage. Such a measure is indemnified as a measure within the meaning of 1.3,
that is, by reference to what it achieves.

The charge for a measure is taken to cover everything deployed in order to
achieve it, including the labour and the working equipment used. Working
equipment brought to the insured site in order to carry out a measure is
therefore not separately indemnified alongside the charge for that measure, and
this holds however the equipment is described, whether it is charged as a hire,
a deployment, a supply or a procurement, and whether the contractor already owned
it or obtained it for the occasion.

Where a measure is charged but the operation it achieves is not, only one of the
two is indemnified; the charge for the measure prevails.

5.2.3 Moving and protecting property
Costs incurred in moving, altering or protecting other property, reimbursable
where those measures serve to reinstate or replace insured property.

5.2.4 Lost water, gas, heating oil and stored electricity
Costs arising because water, gas or heating oil escaped contrary to its intended
purpose as a result of an insured event. Additional wastewater charges fall under
this head.

5.2.5 Hotel costs
Costs of accommodation in a hotel or similar, excluding incidentals such as
breakfast. The precondition is that the dwelling permanently occupied by the
policyholder has become uninhabitable and that confining themselves to a
habitable part of it cannot reasonably be expected of them. The loss of use of an
ancillary or technical room that is not itself living accommodation does not
render a dwelling uninhabitable within the meaning of this head.

5.3 Loss of rent and rental value

The insurer reimburses loss of rent where tenants of residential premises have
lawfully stopped paying rent in whole or in part on account of an insured event,
and the locally customary rental value of residential premises occupied by the
policyholder itself where, on account of the insured event, the policyholder
cannot reasonably be expected to use at least parts of the dwelling.

5.4 The period for loss of rent and rental value

Loss of rent or rental value is reimbursed for the period during which the rooms
are unusable, but for no longer than [number] months from the occurrence of the
insured event, and only to the extent that the policyholder has not culpably
delayed the resumption of use.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 6 - BASIS OF COVER AND PREMIUM
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

6.1 Insurable value

The insurable value forms the basis for calculating the indemnity. The insurable
value determined for the building applies equally to building accessories,
terraces and further site installations.

6.2 Index-linked reinstatement value with enhancement

What is insured is the locally customary new-build value of the insured property
identified in the schedule, taken at the time of the insured event, together with
the additional costs arising from public-law restrictions on reinstatement and
the price increases arising between the occurrence of the insured event and
reinstatement initiated without delay.

6.3 Index-linked current value with enhancement where reinstatement is omitted or
    delayed

For property that is not reinstated, or is reinstated late, only the index-linked
current value with enhancement is insured - the enhanced new-build value at the
time of the insured event, less depreciation for age and for the degree of wear.

6.5 How the premium is calculated

The bases for calculating the premium are the area, the building type, the
construction and the fit-out, the use, other agreed features material to the
premium calculation, and the adjustment factor.

6.6 Adjustment of cover and premium

Where cover is adjusted in line with the development of building costs, the
premium changes accordingly, by way of the adjustment factor taking effect from
1 January of each year.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 7 - CALCULATION AND PAYMENT OF THE INDEMNITY
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

7.1 Basis of calculation

7.1.1 The insurer reimburses:
  (a) for destroyed buildings - the locally customary reinstatement costs, taken
      at the time of the insured event;
  (b) for damaged buildings and other damaged property - the necessary repair
      costs at the time of the insured event, capped at the insurable value at
      that time;
  (c) for destroyed or lost plant of the building and other property - the
      procurement price for property of the same kind and quality in new
      condition, taken at the time of the insured event, together with the cost
      of installing it and putting it into service.

7.1.5 Extent of the repair
Indemnity is confined to those parts of the insured property that were themselves
affected by the insured event. The affected parts are the rooms, surfaces,
building components, installations and items in which physical damage caused by
the event is established by the loss investigation - by inspection, by
photographic record, or by technical measurement taken at or shortly after the
time of the loss.

Work carried out in a room, on a surface, on a building component, on an
installation or on an item that was not itself affected is not covered. This
applies even where the work is carried out
  (a) so that treated and untreated parts correspond in appearance, colour,
      pattern, format or material;
  (b) for reasons of convenience, or because treating a whole room, surface or
      installation is more economical than treating the affected part of it;
  (c) at the same time as covered work, in the course of it, or as part of the
      same overall project; or
  (d) by the same contractor as the covered work, and invoiced together with it.

Where the parts of one installation form a functional unit within the meaning of
2.4.5, that unit is the affected part, and the elements that have to be renewed
with it are not treated as unaffected parts.

7.1.6 Continuous surfaces
Where only part of a single continuous surface was affected, indemnity extends to
the treatment of the adjoining unaffected sections of that same surface only
where a replacement material corresponding to the original is no longer
obtainable and a visible discontinuity would otherwise remain.

7.1.7 Preparatory and ancillary work
The necessary repair costs under 7.1.1(b) and the replacement costs under
7.1.1(c) include:
  (a) disconnecting, dismantling, taking out and disposing of the affected
      installations, components and finishes;
  (b) the drying, dehumidification and moisture-removal measures necessary before
      the repair can be carried out, and the necessary preparation of the
      substrate or supporting structure;
  (c) materials of a type, quality, grade and specification corresponding to
      those in place immediately before the insured event, including the small
      materials, conductors, terminals, fixings, protective devices and
      comparable consumable items actually built into the covered work, whether
      itemised individually or billed as a materials position;
  (d) where an affected installation cannot economically be repaired and is
      replaced, the work of adapting the immediately adjoining supply, connection
      and discharge elements so far as the dimensions, positions or connection
      points of the replacement require it, together with the work of connecting
      it and putting it into service. Such adaptation is part of putting the
      installation back into service and is not an improvement under 7.1.9;
  (e) the investigatory labour reasonably needed to establish which parts of an
      installation were affected, including the testing of circuits and
      components before they are put back into service;
  (f) the labour of the workers of each trade necessarily deployed on the covered
      work, at the ordinary rate of that trade for the category of worker
      actually deployed, whether billed as one position or as several positions
      covering distinct operations;
  (g) one travel, vehicle or call-out charge per trade invoice.

7.1.8 Outlay that is not a repair cost
The following do not constitute repair costs and are not indemnified, however
they may be described or invoiced:

  (a) measures directed at the general condition, cleanliness, tidiness, upkeep,
      preservation, modernisation or improvement of the insured property, as
      distinct from making good the damage caused by the insured event, and
      treatments or products whose purpose is to protect against future
      influences;

  (b) outlay belonging to a contractor's own business operation rather than to
      the repair - its own tools and consumable small equipment, its own
      diagnostic and measuring devices, the provisioning of its own personnel,
      and general administrative, handling, processing, coordination or project
      management charges levied in addition to itemised labour and materials.
      Working equipment within the meaning of 1.3 belongs to this heading and is
      not separately indemnified; it is covered by the charge for the measure or
      the operation in which it was used, in accordance with 5.2.2. The plant of
      the building within the meaning of 1.3 does not belong to this heading and
      is indemnified as insured property under 7.1.1(c);

  (c) the same item of cost where it is invoiced more than once in respect of the
      same insured event, whether by one contractor or across several trades;
      only the first such charge is indemnified;

  (d) more than one travel, vehicle, call-out, return-visit or re-attendance
      charge on the same invoice. One such charge per trade invoice is
      indemnified, and a second trade instructed on the same insured event has
      its own charge under 7.1.7(g).

7.1.9 No improvement on the pre-loss standard
Reinstatement proceeds on the basis of the type, quality, grade and specification
in place immediately before the insured event. Where a higher specification, a
larger format, a superior material or a premium range is chosen instead,
indemnity is limited to the cost of an equivalent standard-grade replacement
corresponding to what was in place before the loss; the difference is borne by
the policyholder.

A replacement installation that differs in construction, technology or energy
source from the destroyed one is not an improvement within the meaning of this
provision where it performs the same function to the same extent and corresponds
to what is customarily supplied for that function at the time of the
reinstatement. The policyholder is not required to seek out a discontinued or
superseded construction in order to preserve its indemnity, and the technical
advance inherent in what is currently supplied is not deducted.

7.1.10 Combined positions
A combined position within the meaning of 1.3 is indemnified where every
operation, every installation and every part of the insured property that it
covers is itself indemnifiable under these conditions. Where an installation is
renewed as a functional unit under 2.4.5, a position covering the unit and its
associated elements is one such position and is indemnified as a whole.

Where any element of a combined position is not indemnifiable, the position is
not indemnified as it stands. The policyholder may submit the position re-stated
by the contractor in separate lines, each showing the operation or the
installation concerned together with its quantity and its price; the separate
lines are then assessed individually and those that are indemnifiable are
indemnified.

7.4 Costs

Insured costs under Part 5 are reimbursed where it is demonstrated that they were
actually incurred. The indemnity limits agreed for each head are applied.

7.7 Value added tax

Value added tax is reimbursed only if and to the extent that it was actually
incurred on the occasion of the reinstatement or replacement. It is not
reimbursed where the policyholder is entitled to recover input tax.

7.8 Deductible

Deductibles are deducted from the indemnity in the amount agreed.

7.9 When the indemnity falls due

The indemnity falls due once the insurer has conclusively determined the claim as
to its basis and its amount. One month after notifying the loss, the policyholder
may claim as an interim payment the amount that is, on the prevailing assessment,
payable as a minimum.

7.13 Deferral of payment

The insurer may defer payment for as long as there is doubt as to the
policyholder's entitlement to receive payment, official or criminal proceedings
arising out of this insured event are still pending, or a legally required
involvement of a secured lender has not taken place.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 8 - EXPERT DETERMINATION PROCEDURE
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

8.1 Determining the amount of the loss
After an insured event has occurred, the policyholder may require that the amount
of the loss be determined in an expert determination procedure. Insurer and
policyholder may also agree on such a procedure jointly.

8.3 Procedure before the determination
Each party is to nominate one expert in text form - by email, fax or letter, for
example. Before beginning their determinations, the two experts nominate in text
form a third expert as umpire. Where the experts cannot agree on the umpire, it
is appointed by the court with local jurisdiction for the loss location, on the
application of either party.

8.4 Content of the determination
The experts' findings must state a schedule of the destroyed and the damaged
insured property together with the corresponding insurable values at the time of
the insured event, the extent of any installation that has to be renewed as a
functional unit, the reinstatement and replacement costs, the residual values,
and the insured costs and the insured loss of rent or rental value.

8.5 Procedure after the determination
Each expert transmits its findings to both parties simultaneously. Where the two
sets of findings diverge, the umpire decides the points that remain in dispute,
within the limits set by the experts' findings. The findings of the experts, or
of the umpire, are binding on the contracting parties. They are not binding where
it is demonstrated that they manifestly deviate substantially from the true state
of affairs.

8.6 Costs
Unless something else has been agreed, each party bears the costs of its own
expert. The costs of the umpire are borne by the two parties in equal shares.

8.7 Duties remain unaffected
The expert determination procedure does not affect the policyholder's duties.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 9 - POLICYHOLDER DUTIES AND INCREASE IN RISK
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

9.1 Contractually agreed safety requirements before an insured event

9.1.1 Insured property must be kept in proper condition at all times. This
applies in particular to water-carrying installations and equipment. Defects or
damage to such property must be remedied without delay.

9.1.2 Buildings or parts of buildings that are not in use must be inspected
sufficiently frequently at every time of year, and the water-carrying
installations there shut off, drained and kept drained.

9.1.3 During the cold season all buildings and parts of buildings must be heated,
and this must be checked sufficiently frequently.

9.2 Duties after an insured event

The policyholder must avert and mitigate the loss so far as it reasonably can,
and must in particular take the measures needed to stop the escape of water and
to remove standing water without delay. The costs of those measures are
reimbursed under 5.2.2.

9.3 Consequences of a breach of duty

Where the policyholder breaches one of the duties in 9.1 or 9.2, the following
applies, subject to the conditions set out in the general contract provisions:
the insurer is entitled to terminate the contract. It may also be wholly or
partly released from liability.

9.4 Circumstances constituting an increase in risk

An increase in risk subject to notification under the general contract provisions
may exist in particular where a circumstance changes about which the insurer
asked before the contract was concluded; where the building or the predominant
part of it is no longer in use; where construction work renders it predominantly
unusable; or where a commercial operation is taken up or changed within the
building.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 10 - CANCELLATION, SECURED LENDERS, TRANSFER OF OWNERSHIP
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

10.1 Cancellation where a security right has been registered

Where a secured lender has registered its charge over the property, cancellation
of the insurance relationship by the policyholder in respect of the fire peril
group is effective only where the policyholder demonstrated, at least one month
before expiry of the insurance contract, that the property was no longer
encumbered with the charge, or that the secured lender consented to the
cancellation. This does not apply to a cancellation following a disposal of the
property, or to a cancellation in the insured event.

10.2 Legal position following a transfer of ownership

Where the policyholder disposes of the insured property, the acquirer steps into
its place in the insurance contract at the date of registration in the land
register, and from that time takes over the rights and obligations of the
policyholder. Seller and acquirer are jointly and severally liable for the
premium for the insurance period in which the transfer of ownership occurs. The
insurer need only recognise the acquirer's entry once it becomes aware of it.

10.3 Rights of cancellation on a transfer of ownership

The insurer is entitled to cancel the contract as against the acquirer on one
month's notice, that right lapsing if it is not exercised within one month of the
insurer becoming aware of the disposal. The acquirer is entitled to cancel with
immediate effect or with effect from the end of the current insurance period, in
text form, that right lapsing one month after the acquisition. In either case the
seller alone remains liable for payment of the premium.

10.4 Duties of notification

The disposal must be notified to the insurer without delay, in text form, by the
seller or by the acquirer. Where that notification has been omitted, the insurer
is not obliged to pay in the insured event on the conditions set out in the
general contract provisions.

===============================================================================
END OF DOCUMENT

case.description:
Hey, quick summary of the flooding incident.

Heavy rainfall caused the basement to flood with around one meter of water. The heating system stopped working as a result.

The tenants had to stay in a hotel temporarily while the flooding was dealt with and the heating was restored.
